structure: One short ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md, 30 lines in four pieces. A title line naming Sam and 9 November 2026; a one-line preamble saying design questions 13 and 10 were decided by Sam after the waiting-on-design evidence review of the same day; the ruling quoted verbatim as two blockquotes ("Yea I agree drop it." and the three-line shout on address search, which calls templates and address search concept work mixed into "get this done" work and says address search is not something to build yet); then an unquoted paragraph of the main session's own context on the review recommendation, the row's three screen-reader criteria, the prototype's hand-built country search and main's GOV.UK accessible autocomplete. Last, a '## Decided' section of three numbered claims the main session read from the quotes: (1) the country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements, dropping the 'Country search results' label and 'Selected <country>' announcement on live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages, with inc-189 dropped and req-020 out of scope; (2) address search is concept work and parked, add-address pages keep every field shown from the start as main has them, inc-194 deferred and its requirements adopted but parked; (3) Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work with deadline work, so a row is checked for deadline need before it goes to the designer or the build loop and flagged to Sam rather than built, a feature main lacks entirely being the usual sign. The scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. The file has no tables, images or links, and the two blockquotes are the only words of the owner: the context paragraph and the three numbered items are the main session's reading and must be checked against those quotes.

parts.title: The whole ruling file
parts.scope: Every line of ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md, from the title to the end of decided item 3: the preamble, both verbatim blockquotes, the context paragraph and all three numbered decided items. Nothing in the file belongs to another part.
covers: Decided item 1, the country search keeping the accessible autocomplete's own announcements: that no 'Country search results' list label and no 'Selected <country>' announcement are built, that this holds on the live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages, that inc-189 is dropped, that req-020 is out of scope, and that design question 13 no longer goes to the designer. The verbatim support for the drop is the quote 'Yea I agree drop it.'; anything beyond those words (the page list, the Welsh versions, the inc/req dispositions) is inferred and its statement must say what in the quote implies it

Decided item 2, address search parked as concept work: that it is not built for the deadline, that the add-address pages keep every field shown from the start as main has them, that inc-194 is deferred, that its requirements stay adopted but parked, and that design question 10 does not go to the designer now. The verbatim support is 'the address earch aint something we need to build yet' and 'it's not a "get done for our deadline job"'; the add-address field behaviour and the inc-194 disposition are inferred

Decided item 3, the standing rule that Design Release 2.1 mixes concept work with deadline work: that templates and address search are concept work, that a row is checked for deadline need before it goes to the designer or the build loop, that a feature main does not have at all and is shown only in the prototype is the usual sign of concept work, and that such a row is flagged to Sam rather than built. The verbatim support is 'some of the stuff in dr 2.1 (like templates) is concept work, which is mixed in with the "get this done work" making things confusing'; the ask-before-it-goes rule and the main-lacks-it test are inferred

Which report question and conflict each claim answers, in note: design question 13 for item 1, design question 10 for item 2, and the waiting-on-design evidence review of 9 November 2026 that the preamble names

Any point the ruling touches but leaves open, as a gap claim with an empty quote: the quotes decide nothing about templates beyond calling them concept work, name no owner or time for the parked address-search work, and say nothing about the Welsh versions of the dropped announcements

Nothing in the context paragraph (the review recommendation, the prototype's hand-built search having no label, arrow keys not working, the typed country lost without JavaScript, main's autocomplete announcing count, highlighted option and chosen value) is a decision by the owner: record such a point only where a quote supports it, otherwise leave it to the sources it came from
Every ref in the form 'ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md claim <N>' for a decided item, or the quoted blockquote for a claim read straight from the owner's words
